questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to choose an English speaking country, and I had only heard good things about the Australian culture and openness towards new people. I also heard the universities had a high academic level and KU had many exchange partners in Australia, I could choose from.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer:
It was very easy. I had booked a free transfer bus through "Campus Living Villages" which was the on-campus accomodation, I was living at in Parramatta. They waited for me at the airport and took me to campus where I could check in to my room.
A few days later, the university had an orientation day with all information about studying in Australia, and we had plenty of opportunity to ask questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Besides the transfer bus, I had received a tons of emails from the university as well as my accomodation with all the information I needed.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It was a "student village" with a lot of apartments from solos to up to 8 people.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: In our apartments we shared a kitchen but the reception at the village also organized a lot of community dinners with free food.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I lived in a 8 bedroom mixed apartment and it got quite messy and dirty. I would probably choose an apartment with fewer people. However, the "student village" is a great way to meet new people and their is plenty of opportunity to socialize with multiple events and dinners.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It was a little difficult because i needed a rule waiver for two of my subjects, but after reaching out to the university, they were able to help. However, I would recommend setting a lot of time aside to research the subjects and register for them.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They have a site called "class registration" at their website with all the information you need. However, when you research for the subjects, you can´t be 100% sure those subjects will actually be availbale your semester, so choose more than the subjects you need.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Assistent from the university through email and the Student Hub at campus.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got into all the classes i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Make sure you choose the right level. Level 1 is first year, level 2 is second and so on. One of my subjects was level 3, which was definitely harder than my other subjects.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The academic level is easier but they have a way more practical approach to studying than I was used to. We didn´t really dive into a lot of theory but we had a lot of case works and projects throughout the semester. I also think they were very generous with the grades.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: We had a lot of self studying , where we had to watch a few "Lecture pods" before every module. They are basically prerecorded lectures, and I really though they were much easier to learn from than the readings. We had a few readings but we didn´t really talk about them in class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
"Looking at Global Politics Through Film"
"Media Cultures"
"Public Relations Theory and Practice"
"Pitch: Podcasting Essentials"

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitely recommend 	"Pitch: Podcasting Essentials". You get to make your own podcast and the teachers were really great at giving good feedback. You also learn a lot about editing, recording, interviewing and storytelling.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I travelled quite a lot within Australia so my personal spending got a little higher than i expected. Also, the supermarkets were often even more expensive than in Denmark.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: They had different social clubs and events and it was also possible to join the different sport teams, but you had to pass the try outs for most of them.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the different events at the university or the "Out and About" club which hosted a lot of trips around Sydney.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go to other places in Australia as well. Flight tickets are pretty cheap and it is also easy to rent a car or take a bus.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy because I lived with people who were all in the same situation as me, so their was always something to do and see and people to see it with. We were also 3 Danish exchange students at the same campus and "student village" which was also really nice.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to them in class and ask if they want to study together or grab a coffee. I found it very easy to socialize with the local students because they are so open and very easy to be around.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The Australians have a different relationship with time so a lot of studens would show up late for class and other things in general.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The openness and friendliness. The Australians are some of the nicest people who would go out of their way to help you, and they love to chat to new people and learn about new cultures.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Live with other exchange students
2. Make sure you explore the country
3. Set aside more money than you think

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You don´t have to figure everything out about your classes before arriving, since you have time to change your subjects once you arrive and start school. So don´t stress yourself out:-)

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: All the people i met!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Different cleaning standards at my accommodation than I am used to.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
